ops.title: A brew-free test PATH cannot make a tool absent — CI puts git and gh in /usr/bin
ops.body:
`internal/vcstest`'s `systemPATH` is `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` — brew-free
by design, so a developer's Homebrew git/jj cannot answer where CI's would not.
It keeps tools OUT of the fixture. It cannot keep a tool out that lives IN one of
those four directories.

That asymmetry is invisible locally and fires on CI:

| tool | dev machine | ubuntu-latest CI |
|---|---|---|
| git | /opt/homebrew/bin (excluded) | **/usr/bin (included)** |
| gh  | /opt/homebrew/bin (excluded) | **/usr/bin (included)** |
| gt  | /opt/homebrew/bin | $HOME/.npm-global |
| jj  | /opt/homebrew/bin | installed outside systemPATH |

So a test asserting a tool is ABSENT passes locally and fails on CI. Measured
2026-08-03: `TestVcsInfoWithoutGh` went red with
`gh resolved to /usr/bin/gh; the fixture PATH must hold none`.

**The rule: a test that needs a tool absent must set an EXCLUSIVE PATH, never
rely on the brew-free one.** Two working idioms already in this repo:

- `t.Setenv("PATH", t.TempDir())` — an empty directory, when the test needs no
  tools at all (`gtrun_test.go`, `TestGTRunReportsAGtThatCannotRun`).
- `t.Setenv("PATH", f.ShimBin)` — the fixture's shim directory ALONE, when the
  test still needs the shimmed tools. `Fixture.ShimBin` is exported for this.
  Verified: read-only git queries work fine with no system directory on PATH.

Worth noting because it cuts against the grain of the de-faking work: the PATH
shell fake this test was converted FROM set `PATH` to its own bin dir
exclusively (`shipfixture_test.go:451`), so it was strictly MORE isolated on this
one axis than the real fixture that replaced it. Converting to real tools buys
honesty about what a tool emits; it does not automatically buy isolation, and
absence is the case where the two pull apart.
